RE-VERIFIED fresh this iteration against HEAD fecba519. The prior iter-1 universal claim ('a humanized label always contains a space or an uppercase letter') FAILed on pure-digit tokens ('2024'->'2024', no space and no uppercase). The docstring now (src/sqllens/tools/_format.py:97-101) states a true, exhaustive two-branch disjunction: a humanized label EITHER contains a space or an uppercase letter (passthrough branch returns it as-is) OR maps to itself under the transform (e.g. a pure-digit word like 2024), so feeding it back returns it unchanged. Traced to code: multi-word snake input yields a space; a single letter-bearing word yields an uppercase via str.capitalize(); the only remaining unchanged form is a pure-digit word which maps to itself (capitalize()/upper() are no-ops on digits). No snake_case input produces a differing snake_case output. Was the sole iter-1 REJECT driver; now PASS.
